title: listscroll tiles
description: Every tile a page of the world can hold, keyed by the tile's name. A page is 256 pixels across and 256 lines down. A tile is a list of pieces: straight runs of identical steps in one of Cyberun's directions, with its step sizes. Rock is decided down each world column: sky above the world, and every floor or ceiling crossing the column turns sky to rock or rock to open. So sky, solid rock and a shaft through rock are all tiles with no pieces; they get their own names because the pieces that draw a page's edges belong to its tile. See build.py.

mirroredFrom.description: Another tile's pieces, mirrored left to right in the page.

upsideDownFrom.description: Another tile's pieces, turned upside down in the page: floors become ceilings.

x.description: The piece's left end, in pixels from the page's left edge.

y.description: The surface's line at the piece's left end: the first line of the side it turns to (rock below a floor, open below a ceiling).

direction.description: Cyberun's directions, without its walls (a wall is where a surface stops). Flat steps are 8 pixels long here (Cyberun's are 24); gentle slopes 16 across and 8 up, plain ones 8 and 8, steep ones 8 and 16. Floors have rock below, ceilings open below; 'up' climbs to the right, 'down' falls to the right.
